items.title: Will AI Coding Eat Video Game Engines?
items.summary: When Travis McGeathy’s studio, Seeker Entertainment, ran out of funding in September, its game KinForge went down with it. KinForge was an online game built in Unreal Engine 5.7 and designed to run on servers hosted by Amazon Web Services (AWS). With no one left to pay the server bill, the game became unplayable even for those few developers, including studio co-founder McGeathy, who had the code. Then, on a whim, McGeathy pointed Anthropic’s Claude Code at the project and asked it to make KinForge playable without AWS. After four hours of mostly hands-off work he had a build that let players…

items.title: Meet Shepherd, the Meta-Agent Keeping Rogue AI In Check
items.summary: AI agents are running amok on the internet, armed with commands to accomplish certain tasks but often acting in undesirable or unexpected ways. These rogue incidents run the gamut from deleting an entire email inbox to hacking websites and even launching cyberattacks . Much like human workers need managers, Weiyan Shi , an assistant professor at Northeastern University , believes AI agents require oversight. “They are running potentially for a long time. items.title: Why a Computer Scientist Thinks Superintelligence Won’t Happen
items.summary: Many people were caught off guard this past summer when employees of one of the world’s leading AI companies began casually debating whether their products would lead to human extinction. items.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
items.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.
